## Exam information

| | Details |
|---|---|
| **Date and time** | Tuesday, December 22, 2026 · 5:30–7:30 pm |
| **Location** | **MEC 3-3**, as listed in the [syllabus](../syllabus/index.qmd#assessment) |
| **Course weight** | 40% |
| **Format** | Two hours, open book; one short-answer question and three practical problems |

Bring a laptop or tablet, a pen or pencil, and any notes or printed materials you wish to consult. The course website, notebooks, assignment solutions, and Python/API documentation are permitted. Search engines may be used for documentation or debugging information.

**Generative AI and communication with other people are prohibited**, including AI assistance in searches, debugging, or writing code.

**Only answers on the answer sheet will be marked.** Show your method, calculations, results, units, and assumptions. Unless a question specifies a method, you may use pen and paper, a calculator, or Python.

**Upload any code through Canvas for record keeping.** If uploading fails, write the key code on the answer sheet. Code quality is not graded.

**No official formula sheet is provided. You may bring your own.**

If a question is unclear, state your interpretation or assumptions and proceed. Ask for technical help if you cannot access the coding environment.

## Mock final examination

The mock has four questions worth 100 points: Q1 (20), Q2 (25), Q3 (30), and Q4 (25). It includes short answers and three problems on linear systems, ordinary differential equations, and numerical integration. Attempt it in two hours under examination conditions.

- [Question paper (PDF)](final-mock.pdf)
- [Q2 · Balancing a chemical reaction (editable notebook)](../wasm-local/final_mock_q2.html){target="_blank"}
- [Q3 · Cooling a steel plate (editable notebook)](../wasm-local/final_mock_q3.html){target="_blank"}
- [Q4 · Length of a pretzel (editable notebook)](../wasm-local/final_mock_q4.html){target="_blank"}

Q2 opens a blank notebook with marimo and NumPy imported. Q3 provides a forward Euler helper that you can use to estimate the cooling time. Q4 provides placeholders for the two coordinate functions and plots the curve automatically once you implement them. Use **Save** or Ctrl+S / Cmd+S to download your edited notebook.
